YOUR ITEMS (interference effects; logcat of the crash: docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/crash-RF8Y30L038L-interference-new-ink-look.txt):
1) CRITICAL: the 'דיו' (ink) hit kills the receiver's JS runtime: "ReferenceError: Property 'INK' doesn't exist at inkPose_inkModelTs1 ... useDerivedValue mapperRun", then React Native destruction (blank dark screen, the player abandons). inkPose() in apps/mobile/src/components/interference/inkModel.ts is a worklet that reads a module-level const INK that the Reanimated/worklets plugin does not capture in the release bundle. Fix the root cause, and AUDIT every other worklet in apps/mobile/src (interference, board, avatars, animations) for the same pattern (worklet reading a module-level object/const that isn't captured, or calling a non-worklet helper). Add a test that fails on the old code: e.g. a static check that worklet functions in these files don't reference module-level identifiers that aren't inlined, or run the plugin transform in Jest and assert the closure contains INK. Don't rely on Jest's worklet mock alone (it runs worklets as plain JS, which is why the tests missed it).
2) MAJOR: warp ('עיוות') hit on the receiver: ~160 ms where the whole app content goes black, then ~260 ms of a static warped frame with no banner/dim, before the banner and dim show. Find why (a heavy first frame: shader/Skia surface creation, a snapshot of the board, a view that mounts opaque before its content is drawn) and make the hit start without a black frame — e.g. pre-warm, mount the effect transparent until its first frame is ready, or show banner/dim first. Respect Reduced Motion.
3) minor: hit banner ring number freezes on '2' for ~1.7 s and '1' shows ~0.3 s while the arc keeps moving smoothly (receiver made a move during the hit). Drive the number from the same clock as the arc (UI thread / derived from the hit's end time), not from a JS tick that the move's work starves.
4) minor: on the SENDER, the launch toast ('<kind> ← <target>') covers the top HUD and both avatars for ~2 s, so the sender's own ~1.5 s wink is never visible. Place/shape the toast so the sender's avatar stays visible (or delay the wink until the toast is gone), keeping the toast readable; RTL and large text.

items.id: 1 CRITICAL interference-new-ink-look: the ink hit kills the receiver's JS runtime (ReferenceError: Property 'INK' doesn't exist at inkPose_inkModelTs1)
items.rootCause: inkPose() is a worklet with default parameters that read the module constant INK (splatMs = INK.splatMs, fadeMs = INK.fadeMs). I ran Expo's Babel preset with the worklets plugin, the same transform Metro uses for the APK. The worklet code it builds is 'function inkPose_inkModelTs1(blot,t,totalMs,splatMs=INK.splatMs,fadeMs=INK.fadeMs){const{INK}=this.__closure;...}'. The closure is read in the body, but default parameters run before the body, so INK does not exist yet on the UI runtime. Ink.tsx calls inkPose with three arguments, so the defaults always ran and the crash hit every receiver. Jest runs worklets as plain JS, where INK is in module scope, so the tests could not see it. The audit covered every worklet in apps/mobile/src, apps/mobile/app and packages/avatars/src: 199 worklets in 110 files. It found the same latent pattern in components/player/format.ts: formatScore and scoreText read DEFAULT_DECIMAL in a default parameter. Every UI-thread caller today passes the separator, so it had not crashed yet. Every function of ours that a worklet calls through its closure is itself a worklet. The other calls go to package APIs (Skia createPicture, scheduleOnRN, interpolate, interpolateColor).
items.fix: inkModel.ts: inkPose takes splatMs?/fadeMs? and resolves them in the body (splatMs ?? INK.splatMs). format.ts: formatScore and scoreText take decimal? and resolve it in the body (decimal ?? DEFAULT_DECIMAL). Behaviour and signatures are otherwise unchanged.
items.test: New apps/mobile/src/__tests__/workletClosures.test.ts (node env). It transforms every file that has worklets with babel-preset-expo (Metro caller, android, release), reads each worklet's code string from the plugin's init data, and checks two things: (1) no worklet parameter reads a closure name; (2) every function of ours that a worklet calls through its closure resolves (through imports and re-exports) to a function with a 'worklet' directive. It also asserts the analysis is not vacuous: more than 150 worklets, inkPose and hitAlpha among them, and inkPose resolves as a worklet while inkPlan does not. On the old code it fails with exactly inkModel.ts inkPose (INK) and format.ts formatScore/scoreText (DEFAULT_DECIMAL); it passes now. Interference, player and decimalSites suites are green.
items.deviceCheck: Two phones, ranked 2P fast, Hebrew. The sender is level 3 or higher with 2+ points. Tap 'הפרעה' on the opponent's card, then 'דיו'. On the receiver: the banner with the sender's avatar and ring, five blots splashing over the board one after another, then fading over the last 1.5 s. The app keeps running and the board stays playable under the blots; no blank dark screen, and logcat has no 'Property 'INK' doesn't exist'. Repeat with system Reduced Motion on: the same blots, still, for 5 s. Also check a score count-up: a negative score shows '−2', not '2−', and English and German separators are unchanged.

items.id: 2 MAJOR interference-hit-warp-look: ~160 ms black content, then ~260 ms frozen warp frame with no banner or dim at the start of a warp hit (receiver)
items.rootCause: Not reproduced off-device; this is the most likely mechanism, and it matches the frames. The hit's start cue plays the kind's sound (hitWarp, hitInk…). sfx builds a sound's player on its first play. expo-audio constructs that player on the UI thread while the JS thread waits (runBlocking; docs/PERF.md already measured this as no frame for ~400 ms on the first play). The game screen preloads only GAME_CUES, and none of the six hit sounds (nor the sender's 'launch' / 'arsenalOpen') were ever preloaded. So the first hit of each kind in a run froze both threads right as the hit layer mounted. The recording matches this. One frame was drawn mid-mount with the content gone. Then a static frame showed the Skia overlay but no banner, dim or tilt, because their animations and the hit clock could not advance. The sender's score update (a JS commit) also arrived only after the stall, at 3.04 s. A second, smaller cause: useHitClock kept the previous hit's elapsed value after a hit ended. This receiver had taken fireworks and cats earlier, so at the next hit's first frames the banner's fade and the dim read the old hit's end (alpha 0) until the new start reached the UI thread.
items.fix: New screens/game/hit/warmHitCues.ts with useWarmHitCues(view.rules), called once in GameScreen next to preloadCues(). In a game with interferences, 1.5 s after mount it makes the players for each allowed kind's start cue, plus 'arsenalOpen' and 'launch'. It makes one player per idle moment (reusing warmGameLater), never several in one stall, and nothing with sound off or in a practice without interferences (D44). hitClock.ts: when a hit goes off, elapsed is reset to 0, so the next hit never starts from the last one's end. Reduced Motion is unaffected: these are sound-player and clock changes only.
items.test: New apps/mobile/src/screens/game/hit/__tests__/warmHitCues.test.tsx renders a GameScreen duel. With interferences on, after the delay, preloadCues is called for hitFireworks, hitCats, hitWarp, hitInk, arsenalOpen and launch, one cue per call. A practice (no interferences) and sound off make none. On the old code no hit cue was ever preloaded, so it fails. HitBanner.test.tsx adds 'the next hit's clock starts from 0' (useHitClock: 3000 during a hit begun 3 s ago, 0 after it ends; the old code keeps 3000).
items.deviceCheck: Cold-start the app with sound on. Join a 2-player friends room or ranked game, play normally, and wait at least 3 s after the board appears. As the FIRST hit of the run, the sender sends 'עיוות'. Record the receiver with screenrecord and step through at 20 ms. There should be no frame with the game content gone. The tilt, the brown overlay, the banner (dropping in) and the board dim start together within a frame or two, and the clock keeps moving. Repeat with 'דיו' and 'זיקוקים' as first hits, and on the receiver's second hit of the same game (the banner and dim must fade in from the start, not pop). On the sender, the first launch should close the picker smoothly with no ~0.4 s freeze. With sound off nothing changes visually. If a black frame still appears, capture logcat around the hit (look for long Choreographer 'Skipped N frames' and AudioPlayer creation) and report back.

items.id: 3 minor interference-hit-banner: the ring number freezes on '2' for ~1.7 s and '1' shows ~0.3 s while the arc drains smoothly
items.rootCause: The arc is an animated prop driven by the hit's UI-thread clock (elapsed). The number was a React <Text> with the `seconds` prop, which comes from the game screen's 250 ms JS tick (useNow). A move during the hit (score count-up, flight, live region, the move's re-renders) starved the JS thread, so the number waited for renders that came late while the arc kept moving.
items.fix: HitBanner: the number is now an animated, read-only TextInput (the CountUpText pattern). Its text is ringSeconds(elapsed, totalMs, screenSeconds), a worklet that computes whole seconds left, rounded up like hitSeconds, from the same clock as the arc. It never shows more than the screen's own seconds, which reach it as a shared value. When the clock has not started, or stands at the end during the fade-out, the screen's value wins, so it never shows 0. The number has a fixed ring width and is centred, so a digit change needs no layout. It is hidden from screen readers; the banner's alert label still says the time left. With Reduced Motion the ring still drains and counts down, as the spec says.
items.test: New apps/mobile/src/screens/game/hit/__tests__/HitBanner.test.tsx. ringSeconds unit cases: 5/4/1 by the clock; screen stale at 2 with the clock at 4.2 s gives 1; part-way start gives the screen's 3; the end keeps 1. A render test with a controlled shared clock: the screen still says 5, the clock moves to 4200 ms, and the number shows '1'. The old code renders a plain Text, so this fails. It also checks a new screen value is followed and that the number is hidden from a11y. HitLayer.test.tsx ring assertions now read the animated text (same expected digits); all 82 hit tests pass.
items.deviceCheck: Friends room, 2 players. The sender launches 'זיקוקים'. About 2.5 s into the hit, the receiver selects an empty cell and enters a correct digit. Record the receiver at 100 ms steps: the ring number shows 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 for about 1 s each (no '2' for 1.7 s), changing in step with the arc. Check the digit is gold and centred in the ring in Hebrew and English, and at font scale 1.3 on a 360 dp width. With TalkBack, the banner is still read as one alert with the time left, and the number is not a separate stop.

items.id: 4 minor avatars-react-hit-sender: the sender's launch toast covers the top HUD and both avatars for ~2 s, so the sender's ~1.5 s wink is never seen
items.rootCause: The sender's confirmation used the generic ToastViewport position: top, under the safe area plus 8, full width. That is exactly over the duel/group HUD's avatar row and scores. motion.md `sender.toast` specifies 'Chip … under my card'. The wink (AVATAR_REACTIONS.on.hitSent, ~1.5 s) and the score paying the cost played under the toast for its whole 240 + 2000 + 240 ms.
items.fix: toastStore ToastContent gets an optional `top` (window coordinates); ToastViewport uses it instead of insets.top + 8 when set. Every other toast is unchanged. useSenderFeedback's InterferenceSent gets an optional `top` and passes it through. GameScreen passes the HUD's bottom + space[2] from its measured layout (layouts.current.hud), so the chip sits under the cards. That is over the lead bar and lock strip; the 62 dp gap to the board holds the 40 dp chip, so it never reaches the board. If the HUD is not measured yet, the chip goes at the old top. The toast's look, size, single line, RTL and large-text behaviour are unchanged, and no strings changed.
items.test: New apps/mobile/src/screens/game/__tests__/senderToast.test.tsx renders GameScreen (duel, interferences on) together with ToastViewport, lays out the HUD at y 48 / height 160, earns 2 points and interferes. The store's toast has top 212 and the viewport renders at top 212. On the old code `top` is undefined and the viewport uses the safe-area top, so it fails. A second case checks a regular toast still sits at the safe-area top. Toast, arsenal (useSenderFeedback) and the GameScreen duel, group and online suites pass.
items.deviceCheck: Ranked 2P, Hebrew. On the sender, tap 'הפרעה' and pick any kind, e.g. 'מספרים מתערבלים'. The dark chip '<kind> ← <target>' slides in just under the two cards, over the lead bar and the 'בחר משבצת' strip, and does not touch the board's top row. Both avatars and scores stay visible: my avatar winks for ~1.5 s, and my score counts down by the cost with the '−N' chip. Repeat in English and at 360 dp / font scale 1.3: the chip is one readable line. In a 3–4 player game the chip sits under the card grid. A blocked 'הפרעה' tap still shows its reason toast at the top as before.

items.id: friends-manage-block-mid-game (MAJOR): app killed mid friends game, relaunch -> 4002 x3 -> 'לא חזרת למשחק בזמן'
items.rootCause: Server side, apps/server/src/rooms/GameRoom.ts onJoin (the game phase). When the process dies, the socket closes without a goodbye. onDrop then holds the seat for the old connection's reconnection token (allowReconnection), and seat.sessionId keeps the OLD session id until the hold runs out. The hold runs out at the abandonment deadline. A cold start has no token, so the app comes back with a new ticket from POST /v1/rooms/join and consumeSeatReservation. GameRoom.onJoin then refused it with `if (seat.sessionId !== null) throw alreadyInRoom`. Colyseus closes that join with 4002 (WITH_ERROR). The app's retries at 4 s and 10 s hit the same refusal, the grace ran out, and the result was abandonment. The new test reproduces it exactly: 'ServerError: alreadyInRoom: <id> is connected already'. The comment in the client (remoteGameHost tryOnce) says the server lets the earlier connection go, but the game phase never did. Only the lobby phase did (FriendsRoom takeover). Ranked has the same server bug. A ranked match room also sets maxClients = the number of human seats, so the held seat locks the room and a rejoin by room id is refused 'room is locked'. Ranked on the phone: the app keeps nothing of a ranked game across a process kill. friendsDevice/useAuthGate keep only a friends room, so after a relaunch the ranked player lands on Home and is never sent back.
items.fix: GameRoom.ts: (1) A new holdSeat(client, seconds) replaces the three allowReconnection calls (onDrop, holdSeatBeforeGame, holdSeatAfterGame). It keeps each hold's reject in `heldSeats` (by session), and onReconnect and onLeave clear the entry. (2) onJoin in the countdown, game or over phase: the seat of the same identity is held for a dropped connection, so the new connection takes it over. The hold is let go; Colyseus then calls onLeave for the old session, which finds no seat. The seat gets the new session, away=false, gate.newSession, and welcomeBack (a fresh snapshot, then the engine's reconnect, so the opponent sees playerReconnected). A connection that is still open is still refused alreadyInRoom, because the server has not seen it drop yet, and the app retries. (3) A match room's maxClients is now 2 × its human seats (dev rooms unchanged, still locked when full). A held seat no longer locks the room, so a rejoin by room id with the same account gets back in. No client change was needed for friends: the cold-start resume (roomToResume → joinByCode(code,'resume') → consumeSeatReservation) now works. NOT DONE (ranked on the phone): the app has no 'resume a ranked game after the app was killed' path. It would need the match room id, game type and players' cards saved on the phone, and the game entered again by room id at start-up, across useAuthGate, gameStore, onlineSession and the game screen. That is a new feature, not a one-line fix, and touches files other agents are editing. The server is ready for it.

Docs: 01-SPEC §5.4 seat line and design/components.md seat line updated (the rating of the room's type, it follows the host's type).

items.id: friends-game-countdown (minor): GO! not shown on the joiner; '1' fades straight to the board
items.rootCause: Client: apps/mobile/app/friends/room.tsx and src/screens/friends/roomPhase.ts. The friends route counted 3-2-1-GO from the server's startsAt against the phone's synced server clock. It opened the game screen (router.replace('/game')) the very moment the room's phase became 'game', which happens when the snapshot arrives at the server's GO. When the phone's count ran even slightly behind the server (clock offset larger than the network delay; this was the joiner), the snapshot came while the screen still said '1'. The route then switched at once: roomScreenPhase gave 'starting' and the route replaced to /game in the same commit. So no GO! frame, and the '1' faded onto the board. The host's count happened to reach GO first. The ranked flow (MatchScreen) already shows GO! when the board comes before the phone's own GO and holds it goHoldMs; the friends flow did not.
items.fix: roomPhase.ts: phase 'game' after a count this connection saw (room.startsAt set) now gives the countdown at step 'go': GO! with 'מכינים את הלוח…', whatever the phone's own count says. A game entered again without a count (resume) stays 'starting'. New friendsGoHoldMs(reduce, os) holds GO + 400 ms (motion tokens sequence.matchFound), less the game screen's own fade (flowFadeMs): 250 ms on Android, also with Reduced Motion. It is the same formula as the ranked goHoldMs. room.tsx: it notes in phone time when GO! first shows, and opens /game only once GO! has held friendsGoHoldMs. If GO! already showed long enough before the board came, the game opens at once, as before. The 'go' cue plays on every phone. Android back stays held during GO (the phase kind is still 'countdown'). No new strings. Reduced Motion: GO! still shows (the Step slam is already reduced-motion aware), with the shorter fade.

items.id: network-abandon-countdown (minor): opponent-freeze ring stops on 1, never 0 or 'הזמן נגמר / בודקים מול השרת…'
items.rootCause: Checked spec §16.2 and D4/D42: the grace countdown runs on the server, and everyone sees the same graceEndsAt. The client's ring (connectionModel.ts, opponentReconnecting) is remainingMs = graceEndsAt − serverNow, with secondsOf = ceil. So '1' is the last whole second, from graceEndsAt−1000 up to graceEndsAt. The server's engine timer ends the grace at exactly graceEndsAt, and its gameOver arrives one network delay later. What was recorded, '1' on screen for about 1 s and then straight to 'ניצחת בנטישה', is that timeline exactly, so the local count and the server are aligned. items.rootCause: inkPose() is a worklet whose default parameters read the module constant INK (splatMs = INK.splatMs, fadeMs = INK.fadeMs). I ran Expo's Babel preset with the worklets plugin, the same transform Metro uses for the APK. The worklet code it builds is 'function inkPose_inkModelTs1(blot,t,totalMs,splatMs=INK.splatMs,fadeMs=INK.fadeMs){const{INK}=this.__closure;...}'. The closure is read in the body, but default parameters run before the body, so INK does not exist yet on the UI runtime. Ink.tsx calls inkPose with three arguments, so the defaults always ran and every receiver crashed. Jest runs worklets as plain JS, where INK is in module scope, so the tests could not see it. I audited every worklet in apps/mobile/src, apps/mobile/app and packages/avatars/src: 199 worklets in 110 files. The same latent pattern was in components/player/format.ts: formatScore and scoreText read DEFAULT_DECIMAL in a default parameter. It had not crashed yet because every UI-thread caller passes the separator. Every function of ours that a worklet calls through its closure is itself a worklet. The other calls are package APIs.

items.id: 2 MAJOR interference-hit-warp-look: ~160 ms black content, then ~260 ms frozen warp frame with no banner or dim at the start of a warp hit (receiver)
items.rootCause: Not reproduced off-device. The reviewer is right that the sound stall alone cannot draw a black frame, so this round I split the symptom in two. (a) The ~260 ms frozen frame with no banner and no dim is explained. The kind's start sound was never preloaded, and expo-audio builds a player on the UI thread while JS waits, so no frames and no JS run (docs/PERF.md). Also, HitLayer's hit clock kept the previous hit's end after fireworks and cats. HitBanner's opacity is enter × hitAlpha(elapsed, total, 0, fadeOut), so a stale elapsed = total gives 0 for the banner, and BoardHitLayer's dim is also 0, until the new start lands. (b) The ~160 ms black frame is specific to the warp's own tilt. The QA text says only the status bar, the nav bar and the ambient digits stayed. The ambient digits are an opaque Skia canvas mounted in the root layout, outside the game screen's WarpFrame. So only the content inside WarpFrame region='screen' stopped drawing. Fireworks and cats mount the same kind of Skia canvas in HitLayer and did not flash. Warp is the only kind that changes the content view's own transform (perspective + rotateX/Y/Z + scale), and before this round it began on the hit's very first frame, together with the mount, the cue and the haptic. I ruled out NaN or degenerate values, a stale clock on the frame (it was never warped, so elapsed was 0), and Fabric view flattening (the NO_WARP transform is never empty, so the view always forms). I could not pin down the exact Android/HWUI mechanism (likely a first-use cost of drawing the whole content under a 3D matrix) without a phone.

items.id: friends-manage-block-mid-game (MAJOR): app killed mid friends game, relaunch -> 4002 x3 -> 'לא חזרת למשחק בזמן'
items.rootCause: Server side, in apps/server/src/rooms/GameRoom.ts onJoin, during the game phase. When the app process dies, the socket closes without a goodbye. onDrop then holds the seat for the old connection's reconnection token (allowReconnection). Until that hold runs out, at the abandonment deadline, seat.sessionId keeps the old session id. A cold start has no token, so the app comes back with a new ticket (POST /v1/rooms/join, then consumeSeatReservation). GameRoom.onJoin refused that ticket with `if (seat.sessionId !== null) throw alreadyInRoom`, and Colyseus closed the join with 4002. The app's retries at about 4 s and 10 s hit the same refusal, the grace ran out, and the game ended as abandoned. Only the lobby phase let an earlier connection go; the game phase never did. Ranked had the same bug, plus one more: a match room set maxClients to the number of human seats, so a held seat locked the room and a rejoin by room id was refused with 'room is locked'. On the phone, the app keeps nothing of a ranked game when the process is killed (friendsDevice and useAuthGate keep only a friends room). So after a relaunch, a ranked player lands on Home.
items.fix:
Changes in GameRoom.ts. (1) A new holdSeat(client, seconds) replaces the three allowReconnection calls (onDrop, holdSeatBeforeGame, holdSeatAfterGame). It keeps each hold's reject in `heldSeats`, keyed by session; onReconnect and onLeave clear the entry. (2) In the countdown, game and over phases, onJoin lets the same identity take back a seat that is held for a dropped connection. The hold is released, and the seat gets the new session with away=false, gate.newSession and welcomeBack (a snapshot, then the engine's reconnect, so the opponent gets playerReconnected). A connection the server still sees as open is still refused alreadyInRoom, and the app retries. (3) A match room's maxClients is now 2 x its human seats, so a held seat no longer locks the room. No client change was needed for friends: the existing cold-start resume (roomToResume, then joinByCode(code,'resume'), then takeFriendsSeat) now gets in.

On the reviewer's half-open TCP concern, I checked whether the client's retries can miss the window. They cannot. Killing the process makes the OS close the socket, so the server sees the drop at once and the first try gets in. If the socket is half-open, the server's heartbeat (apps/server/src/app.ts HEARTBEAT: pingInterval 1500 ms, pingMaxRetries 2) cuts it within 4.5 s, through the same onDrop/hold path. The client's takeFriendsSeat tries at 0, 3, 9 and 21 s after relaunch (friendsHeldSeatDelaysMs 3000/6000/12000/20000). The engine's grace is softGraceMs 10 s + graceMs 15 s = 25 s from the drop. With a relaunch within about 7 s, the tries land at about drop+7, +10 and +16 s, all after the heartbeat window and before the deadline. So no client retry change is needed. I added a server test for exactly this sequence.

NOT DONE, ranked on the phone: the app has no path to resume a ranked game after the process was killed. The server side is ready: the matchmaking test proves a rejoin by room id with the same account gets back into the same game. The phone would need to save the match room id, game type and player cards, and enter the game again from useAuthGate. That touches gameStore, onlineSession, useAuthGate and the game screen. It is a new feature and an open decision for Moshe (see notes).

items.id: 1 (minor): A16 1080x2340 results, the 'שינוי דירוג · מהיר' number and change sit under the 'משחק חדש' / 'צפייה חוזרת' bar, and the old→new count has already run before you scroll to it
items.rootCause: RatingSection started its count on a fixed timer (motion.md rating.count, 1200 ms after the results mount), whether or not the number was on screen. The action bar is a flex sibling below the ScrollView. On a 1080x2340 phone (about 411x891 dp) the hero, the final score and the opponent row push the card's value row below the ScrollView's bottom edge. The count ran there unseen, and when the user scrolled down they saw only the final value.
items.fix: New hook screens/results/useScrolledIntoView.ts. It tracks the ScrollView's height (onLayout) and offset (onScroll, throttled to 16 ms), the rating card's top in the content (wrapper onLayout), and the bottom of the value row inside the card. `below` is false until the layouts are measured, true while the row is under the fold, and false for good once the row has been in view. RatingSection takes `waiting` and `onValueLayout`, and its target becomes `reduce || (started && !waiting) ? after : before`.
